decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Mega Gengar. Aerodactyl + Gengar lead sets Tailwind via Aerodactyl (Focus Sash guarantees setup, Unnerve blocks berries) while Mega Gengar traps with Shadow Tag and applies fast Shadow Ball/Sludge Bomb pressure. Under Tailwind, Mega Gengar outspeeds Scarf Garchomp. Dragonite and Arcanine in back complete the plan: Dragonite's Inner Focus ignores Fake Out and OHKOs Garchomp with Life Orb Ice Spinner, while Arcanine provides Intimidate cycling and Extreme Speed priority.

Strategic notes:
- Scarf Garchomp relies on outspeeding dragon/ghost threats. Tailwind from Aerodactyl completely neutralizes its Scarf speed advantage, enabling Ice Spinner Dragonite and Mega Gengar to sweep.

decisions.rationale: No Mega is intended in this four; Charizard Y is avoided because Aerodactyl’s Sash, Tailwind, Wide Guard, and Rock Slide make its mode unreliable. Raichu disrupts Aerodactyl immediately while Scarf Garchomp forces Mega Gengar respect. Primarina supplies Dragonite pressure; Hisuian Goodra is the durable endgame into special attackers and Clefable.
decisions.notebook: Opponent used offensive Gengar/Aerodactyl/Dragonite/Arcanine in Game 1. Mega Gengar has shown willingness to Protect when threatened by Scarf Garchomp. Aerodactyl is Focus Sash with Tailwind, Taunt, Wide Guard, and Rock Slide; respect it as key disruption and Rock Slide source. Favor Raichu to deny or slow Aerodactyl. Avoid relying on Mega Charizard Y while Aerodactyl Rock Slide pressure remains.

decisions.rationale: Scarf Garchomp outspeeds Gengar and OHKOs with Stomping Tantrum, making Protect + Mega Evolve mandatory on Gengar to safely reveal Garchomp's locked move while setting Shadow Tag. Aerodactyl goes for Tailwind to establish speed control; if Raichu uses Fake Out on Aerodactyl, Sash or typing keeps Aerodactyl alive against Stomping Tantrum targeting Gengar.

Fake Out denies Aerodactyl’s Tailwind or Wide Guard and breaks its Focus Sash. Scarf Garchomp outspeeds both foes at neutral priority and Stomping Tantrum threatens a guaranteed KO on Gengar if it does not Protect. This covers their aggressive line while leaving Aerodactyl easily removable next turn if Gengar protects.

Garchomp is Choice Scarf locked into Stomping Tantrum and outspeeds Gengar-Mega. Switching Gengar-Mega to Flying-type Dragonite completely absorbs the Ground attack for 0 damage. Aerodactyl outspeeds Raichu (200 vs max 178) and sets up Tailwind before Raichu can attack, securing speed control for the rest of the game.

Sending in Mega Gengar activates Shadow Tag, trapping Garchomp (locked into Stomping Tantrum) and Raichu so Garchomp cannot switch out to absorb Dragonite's Ice Spinner. Under Tailwind, both Dragonite (264 Effective Speed) and Mega Gengar outspeed the entire opposing side, guaranteeing a clean OHKO on Garchomp next turn before it can move.

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt always removes the sash-broken Aerodactyl if Raichu acts, while Scarf Garchomp guaranteed OHKOs Mega Gengar through any non-Protect line. This covers Gengar's likely repeat Protect by still removing Aerodactyl and prevents Tailwind/Wide Guard disruption.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar protected immediately against Scarf Garchomp in Game 2 and may repeat Protect when threatened. Aerodactyl's Focus Sash has been broken; its revealed disruption is Tailwind, Taunt, Wide Guard, and Rock Slide. Opponent's Game 1 mode included offensive Gengar/Aerodactyl/Dragonite/Arcanine.

decisions.rationale: Under Tailwind, Dragonite (264 speed) outspeeds Scarf Garchomp (max 253) and guarantees an OHKO with 4x Ice Spinner before Garchomp can execute Stomping Tantrum. Raichu cannot flinch Dragonite due to Inner Focus, nor Gengar-Mega due to Ghost typing. Gengar-Mega (400 speed) moves first overall and chunks Raichu with Sludge Bomb.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp cannot use its locked Ground move into Dragonite and is exposed to Ice Spinner. Protect preserves Raichu through Tailwind while Goodra-Hisui is the sturdier pivot: it resists Sludge Bomb and does not take super-effective damage from Ice Spinner. Preserve Primarina to pressure Dragonite after Tailwind.

Dragonite has Life Orb with ExtremeSpeed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, and Protect; Inner Focus does not prevent paralysis. Aerodactyl is gone. Opponent has shown a fast Tailwind offense mode; prioritize stalling Tailwind and preserve Primarina as the Dragonite answer.

decisions.rationale: Raichu cannot safely act through Tailwind and is threatened by Gengar, while Dragonite can immediately remove Garchomp with Ice Spinner. Protect denies the Sludge Bomb line and preserves Raichu to disrupt Dragonite after Tailwind. Garchomp’s only legal meaningful attack pressures Mega Gengar; Dragonite may act first at its higher legal Speed range.

Dragonite has ExtremeSpeed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, and Protect; Inner Focus does not prevent paralysis. Aerodactyl is gone. Prioritize stalling Tailwind and preserve Primarina as the Dragonite answer.

decisions.rationale: Goodra-Hisui is the safe pivot: it resists Gengar’s Sludge Bomb, whereas Primarina is immediately exposed to a super-effective Sludge Bomb under Tailwind. Preserve Primarina to answer Dragonite after Tailwind is stalled; Goodra can absorb the immediate board pressure better.

Dragonite has ExtremeSpeed, Ice Spinner, Rock Slide, and Protect; Inner Focus does not prevent paralysis. Aerodactyl is gone. Prioritize stalling Tailwind and preserve Primarina as the Dragonite answer. Avoid switching Primarina directly into Mega Gengar while it can use Sludge Bomb.

decisions.rationale: Goodra's Dragon Pulse threatens to KO 78% Dragonite (70.5-102.4% range). Protecting Dragonite blocks Dragon Pulse completely while Tailwind is active. Mega Gengar uses Sludge Bomb on Raichu, dealing 51.5-98.5% damage without taking fatal damage in return. Preserving Dragonite maintains complete board control for Turn 5 under Tailwind.

decisions.rationale: Dragon Pulse removes the Life Orb Dragonite from its shown range while Raichu’s Nuzzle gives the best future disruption against Mega Gengar after Tailwind. Goodra is protected from Sludge Bomb and can absorb Dragonite’s resisted ExtremeSpeed/Rock Slide; preserving Primarina avoids exposing it to Sludge Bomb.

Extreme Speed (+2 priority) guarantees Raichu's KO at 18% HP before it can land Nuzzle on Dragonite or Thunderbolt on Gengar, avoiding Rock Slide's 10% miss risk. Gengar-Mega uses Shadow Ball to chip Goodra-Hisui into range of a 2v1 endgame where both Dragonite (132 Speed) and paralyzed Gengar (100 Speed) outspeed Modest Goodra-Hisui (max 112 Speed) after Tailwind ends.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Raichu must Protect from Dragonite’s priority ExtremeSpeed. Goodra’s Dragon Pulse threatens the 77% Dragonite through its final Tailwind turn; even a successful repeat Protect only buys them a turn while Tailwind expires and preserves Raichu. Gengar cannot stop Dragon Pulse with Sludge Bomb, and Shadow Ball does not prevent Goodra acting.

Arcanine's +2 priority Extreme Speed comfortably finishes the 18% HP Raichu before it can act, removing its offensive threat entirely. Goodra-Hisui cannot OHKO Gengar-Mega with Dragon Pulse (max 65.2% vs 91% HP), allowing Gengar to land Shadow Ball for 24.6-51% chip. This puts Goodra into range for Arcanine's faster Flare Blitz to secure the win next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Game 2 roster: Charizard-Y, Garchomp (Scarf), Raichu (Lum), Goodra-Hisui (Leftovers). Raichu was KOed turn 6. Goodra-Hisui has Flash Cannon/Dragon Pulse/Body Press/Protect.

decisions.rationale: Raichu is guaranteed faster than paralyzed Gengar and chips it before likely falling to Extreme Speed or Sludge Bomb. Goodra Protect denies the key Shadow Ball/Flare Blitz double-up and preserves the Primarina endgame. If Gengar Protects, Goodra still avoids damage while Primarina replaces Raichu.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Arcanine (115 Speed) outspeeds both Modest Primarina and Goodra-Hisui (max 112 Speed). Flare Blitz chunking Goodra-Hisui into range (31.6-56.8%) combined with Gengar-Mega's super-effective Sludge Bomb into Primarina (73.3-127.7%) pressure both slots heavily. Gengar-Mega is immune to Goodra-Hisui's Body Press and resists Primarina's Moonblast.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Game 2 roster: Charizard-Y, Garchomp (Scarf, fainted), Raichu (Lum, fainted), Goodra-Hisui (Leftovers, -1 Atk). Goodra-Hisui has Flash Cannon/Dragon Pulse/Body Press/Protect. Primarina has Life Orb (Hydro Pump/Moonblast/Ice Beam/Protect).

decisions.rationale: Apply immediate split KO pressure: Hydro Pump threatens Arcanine’s guaranteed KO if it does not Protect, while Dragon Pulse is Goodra’s strongest listed attack into Gengar. Gengar is faster even while paralyzed, but attacking both foes prevents either from freely using its key damage move; double Protect is the main defensive response.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar is Timid with Protect, Sludge Bomb, Shadow Ball, and Will-O-Wisp; it was paralyzed by Nuzzle. Arcanine is Impish Intimidate with Flare Blitz, Extreme Speed, Will-O-Wisp, Snarl, and Sitrus Berry. Opponent’s early-game mode used Aerodactyl Tailwind plus Mega Gengar and Life Orb Dragonite; preserve Primarina as the Dragonite answer when Dragonite is available.

decisions.rationale: Goodra-Hisui is at 32% HP and burned; Leftovers and burn damage offset each other. Gengar-Mega is at 35% HP and paralyzed, which places it in KO range of both Dragon Pulse (39.3-46.7%) and Flash Cannon (36.3-43.0%). Shadow Ball is Gengar's only move that can damage Steel/Dragon Goodra-Hisui, dealing 24.6-51.0% which can KO on high rolls if Gengar avoids full paralysis and outspeeds. Protect delays the turn but does not alter the win condition since Goodra has no reason not to attack on the follo
decisions.notebook: Game 2 end state: Goodra-Hisui has Flash Cannon, Dragon Pulse, Body Press, Protect (Leftovers). Gengar-Mega paralyzed at low HP.

decisions.rationale: Gengar is guaranteed faster despite paralysis, and Shadow Ball cleanly KOs Goodra. Protect is the only line that avoids immediate loss, blocks Shadow Ball, and gains Leftovers recovery; then Goodra can threaten the guaranteed Dragon Pulse KO if it survives burn.

Goodra-Hisui is at 32% HP and used Protect last turn. Gengar-Mega at 35% HP par is KO'd by Flash Cannon or Dragon Pulse. If Goodra is slower than 100 Speed, Gengar moves first; Shadow Ball deals 27.3-45.2% and can KO. Protect on turn 9 would allow Goodra to reset its Protect counter for turn 10 without changing the speed order. Shadow Ball into Goodra-Hisui is our best and only line to win.

Goodra must attack now: Dragon Pulse guarantees the KO if it moves, but paralyzed Mega Gengar is still guaranteed faster and Shadow Ball KOs. Protect only delays the same speed problem while burn continues; attacking maximizes the immediate full-paralysis win chance.

reflections.summary: Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag successfully trapped and eliminated Primarina and Goodra-Hisui, but bringing Dragonite into Goodra-Hisui created severe vulnerability; the game was saved when Arcanine's Flare Blitz burned Goodra-Hisui, allowing a paralyzed Gengar to clean up.
reflections.adjustment: Adjust the lead to immediately deny Raichu's Nuzzle before Mega Gengar takes status, and consider benching Dragonite in Game 3 against Goodra-Hisui's super-effective coverage.
reflections.notebook: Goodra-Hisui: Modest, Leftovers (Flash Cannon, Dragon Pulse, Body Press, Protect). Raichu: Timid, Lum Berry (Fake Out, Nuzzle, Thunderbolt, Protect). Primarina: Modest, Life Orb, Liquid Voice (Hydro Pump, Moonblast, Ice Beam, Protect). Garchomp: Jolly, Choice Scarf. Opponent uses Raichu Nuzzle to neutralize Mega Gengar's Speed; lead Arcanine or protect Gengar early to deny status.

reflections.summary: Lost because Primarina was left exposed to Mega Gengar’s Sludge Bomb on turn 7 while trading into Arcanine; the resulting double KO left burned Goodra unable to close out the weakened Gengar. The four brought had workable tools for this mode, but Garchomp’s contribution is not supported by the available evidence, and no evidence identifies an intended Mega on our side to evaluate.
reflections.adjustment: Against Gengar + Arcanine, protect Primarina rather than immediately Hydro Pumping Arcanine, and have Goodra finish the already weakened Gengar. Preserve Primarina for the endgame instead of accepting the Sludge Bomb trade.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s Aerodactyl + Mega Gengar mode uses Tailwind, with Aerodactyl also showing Focus Sash, Wide Guard, and Taunt. Mega Gengar is vulnerable to Nuzzle but is a major Sludge Bomb threat to Primarina; when Gengar is already in Goodra’s Dragon Pulse range, prioritize removing it while protecting Primarina. Arcanine provides Intimidate, Snarl, Will-O-Wisp, and priority pressure. Preserve Primarina rather than trading it into Mega Gengar when it is needed to clean up.
